feed.title: Ebola Tracker: DR Congo
feed.subtitle: Independent, sourced tracker of the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in DR Congo: confirmed cases and deaths, affected provinces, spread to other countries, vaccines, WHO risk and a dated timeline.

entry.title: African health ministers agree to keep borders open
entry.summary: After an extraordinary virtual meeting of African health ministers on 28 October, Africa CDC's director general Jean Kaseya said the ministers agreed to prepare every country, coordinate across borders and keep borders open while watching them closely. He told the meeting the continent is not winning so far, per Anadolu, TRT Afrika and Premium Times.
entry.content:
After an extraordinary virtual meeting of African health ministers on 28 October, Africa CDC's director general Jean Kaseya said the ministers agreed to prepare every country, coordinate across borders and keep borders open while watching them closely. He told the meeting the continent is not winning so far, per Anadolu, TRT Afrika and Premium Times.

Sources: Anadolu Agency (28 Oct), TRT Afrika, Premium Times

entry.title: Kenya releases the first 20 Ebola contacts from quarantine
entry.summary: Kenya's health ministry released the first 20 contacts after 21 days of monitoring without symptoms. Health Director-General Patrick Amoth said the outbreak is not over; the remaining 98 contacts are expected to leave quarantine in four waves from 3 November, based on individual health assessments, Reuters reported.

Sources: Reuters via KSL, Capital FM

entry.title: DR Congo passes 10,000 confirmed Ebola cases
entry.summary: DR Congo's public health institute (INSP) reports 10,060 confirmed cases and 4,887 deaths as of 25 October, in 66 health zones across eight provinces, Reuters and Al Jazeera reported on 27 October. ECDC's update of 25 October, covering data to 24 October, counted 9,964 cases and 4,851 deaths.

DR Congo's public health institute (INSP) reports 10,060 confirmed cases and 4,887 deaths as of 25 October, in 66 health zones across eight provinces, Reuters and Al Jazeera reported on 27 October. ECDC's update of 25 October, covering data to 24 October, counted 9,964 cases and 4,851 deaths.

Sources: Reuters via U.S. News (27 Oct), Al Jazeera (27 Oct), The Watchers (27 Oct), ECDC: Ebola disease, multi-country outbreak 2026

entry.title: CDC lists 9,816 confirmed cases in DR Congo
entry.summary: CDC's situation summary lists 9,816 confirmed cases and 4,757 confirmed deaths in DR Congo as of 22 October, compared with 9,704 cases and 4,687 deaths as of 20 October in WHO's Disease Outbreak News. CDC says confirmed cases are in eight provinces and that case counts are expected to change as investigations continue.

entry.title: Nurse killed in attack on Ebola responders in Tshopo
entry.summary: A nurse was killed and another health worker seriously injured on 24 October in Bafwasende, Tshopo province, while responding to an Ebola alert, WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said, as reported by AP and Al Jazeera. WHO condemned the attack.

Sources: AP via U.S. News, Al Jazeera

entry.title: First participant vaccinated in the Tumaini trial
entry.summary: CEPI said the first participant was vaccinated on 23 October in Bunia, DR Congo, marking the start of Tumaini, a pivotal Phase 2/3 trial of vaccine candidates against Bundibugyo virus run with Epicentre, MSF, WHO and Africa CDC. Bloomberg reported that the first dose was Ervebo, which is licensed for the Zaire species; whether it protects against Bundibugyo is not yet known. Experimental candidates from Moderna and from Oxford with the Serum Institute of India could be added within weeks, Bloomberg reported.

entry.title: Kenya announces a second Ebola death
entry.summary: Kenya's health ministry announced the death of a patient who had been in quarantine, the second death among Kenya's nine confirmed cases. The ministry said all confirmed cases remain within one cluster of known contacts, with no evidence of community spread, and that the other seven patients are receiving care, AP reported.

entry.title: Africa CDC investigates a possible link between the first Kenya and Nigeria cases
entry.summary: Africa CDC said the first patients confirmed in Kenya and Nigeria both passed through Entebbe airport in Uganda on 3 October, and that whether they crossed paths there is one theory being investigated, AP reported. Kenya's health ministry has said all nine of its cases belong to one cluster; Nigeria has placed 44 contacts under follow-up.

Sources: AP via KSAT, Health Policy Watch

entry.title: CDC requires an Ebola attestation for all US-bound air passengers
entry.summary: CDC issued an order requiring every passenger boarding an international flight to the United States, whatever their nationality, to attest that they have not been in DR Congo in the 21 days before boarding. The requirement starts at 11:59 pm Eastern time on 3 November, and airlines must check the attestation before boarding. It adds to CDC's existing entry restrictions for travellers recently in DR Congo, Uganda or South Sudan.
entry.content:
CDC issued an order requiring every passenger boarding an international flight to the United States, whatever their nationality, to attest that they have not been in DR Congo in the 21 days before boarding. The requirement starts at 11:59 pm Eastern time on 3 November, and airlines must check the attestation before boarding. It adds to CDC's existing entry restrictions for travellers recently in DR Congo, Uganda or South Sudan.

Sources: CDC order, NBC News, CNBC Africa (Reuters)

entry.title: Africa CDC calls an extraordinary meeting of health ministers
entry.summary: Africa CDC said it will convene an extraordinary meeting of African health ministers on 28 October to strengthen the collective response to the outbreak, AP reported. Its director general said the outbreak demands urgent action and political leadership at the highest level.
entry.content:

Sources: AP via U.S. News, AP via Medical Xpress

entry.title: Kenya confirms a ninth Ebola case
entry.summary: Kenya's health ministry said one more person tested positive, bringing the total to nine including the first patient, who died. The new case is a contact of the first patient who was already in quarantine. The ministry said all nine cases belong to one cluster, that there is no evidence of transmission outside it, and that 134 of 135 identified contacts were in quarantine. It said the first group of contacts completes 21 days of quarantine on 25 October.

Sources: Al Jazeera, The Washington Post, The Standard (Kenya)

entry.title: Nigeria confirms an imported Ebola case
entry.summary: Nigeria's health ministry confirmed one case of Bundibugyo Ebola in the Federal Capital Territory, in a person with recent travel to Uganda; laboratory confirmation was on 20 October. Officials said 44 contacts had been identified. WHO calls it an imported case and the fifth country to detect the virus since the outbreak was declared, says where and when the person was exposed is not yet known, and advises against restrictions on travel or trade.

entry.title: DR Congo confirms Ebola in an eighth province, North Ubangi
entry.summary: DR Congo's health ministry said on 18 October that the outbreak has reached North Ubangi province, which borders the Central African Republic, with two cases, one of them fatal, in Wapinda health zone. Reuters and Bloomberg had reported the cases on 15 October before the official statement. AP reports the outbreak has recorded at least 9,400 confirmed cases and more than 4,500 deaths, with Ituri province accounting for almost three quarters of cases.

Sources: AP via U.S. News, AP via The Washington Times, Asharq Al-Awsat

entry.title: Kenya confirms four more Ebola cases, total seven
entry.summary: Kenya's health ministry said four more people tested positive, bringing the total to seven including the first patient, who died. Three are health workers who cared for the first patient and one is a relative; all were already in quarantine. The ministry said 128 of 130 identified contacts were in quarantine, that there was no evidence of community transmission and that the risk to the general public remained low.

Sources: Al Jazeera, AP via The Washington Times, Bloomberg

entry.title: Kenya confirms a third Ebola case
entry.summary: Kenya's health ministry said a close contact of the first two patients, who had been in quarantine since 6 October, tested positive. The ministry said there was no evidence of community spread, and contacts continue daily monitoring for 21 days. Kenya now has three confirmed cases and one death.

entry.title: Media report Ebola in an eighth province, North Ubangi
entry.summary: Reuters and Bloomberg report, citing health officials, two confirmed Ebola cases in North Ubangi province, which borders the Central African Republic. Reuters says Congolese authorities had not yet officially announced the cases. It also reports that several suspected Ebola deaths had recently occurred at a mining site in Wapinda health zone, with samples sent for laboratory analysis in the province and in Kinshasa.

entry.title: ECDC: 9,277 cases and 4,478 deaths
entry.summary: ECDC reports 9,277 confirmed cases and 4,478 deaths in DR Congo as of 15 October (data to 14 October), with 924 patients in isolation in hospital. New cases in the latest report were in Ituri (31), North Kivu (28), Haut-Uele (5) and Tshopo (1). ECDC also notes the media reports of cases in North Ubangi.

entry.title: Kenya confirms a second Ebola case
entry.summary: Kenya's health ministry said a relative of the first patient, who was already in quarantine and under daily monitoring, tested positive after developing symptoms on 13 October. The ministry said it identified 128 contacts of the first patient and found no evidence of spread in the community. Kenya now has two confirmed cases and one death.
entry.content:

The ministry said it identified 128 contacts of the first patient and found no evidence of spread in the community. Kenya now has two confirmed cases and one death.

Sources: AP via WRAL, CBC, The Washington Post

entry.title: Africa CDC asks for accountability on over $700 million of response funding
entry.summary: Africa CDC's director general said on 14 October that more than $700 million of Ebola response funding channelled through international partners could not yet be traced to the response, and that the funds were not transferred to the DR Congo government. He asked partners to account for the money, and DR Congo authorities said they would ask the partners concerned for explanations.
